cells.tense: You are at the table now, pen in hand, adjusting the blend as you go.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: The heading you chose for this connection will get questioned. Keep it once without arguing it back into line — let the questioning pass and hold where you pointed yourself.
cells.core: A direction you chose is holding, and you are inside it, adjusting as you go. The adjusting is the evidence. When this is carrying well, you feel the shared direction and your own at the same time — you sense which word to soften, which to let stand, and the two of you stay one current without either bank collapsing. That is the good version, and it is reachable today. Right now you can do it and also carry the residue: a slightly braced ear for the moment the other one pulls. The brace is not a fault in the direction; it is a rehearsal for it. Which means the work here isn't more feeling. It is one clean act of direction, kept.
cells.sheetLine: You are in the flow and already testing its pull.
cells.verb: Crossing into one shared current without losing your own bank
cells.place: The inner table where you sense when to add, when to subtract

cells.tense: It will happen before you have the words, and you are bracing there now.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Think of one thing your care has already grown — between you, or in your own life — and give it a day with your hands off. Don't check whether it has improved since morning.
cells.core: When a connection is forming, you get ahead of it: you feel the future shape of it before it has had its hour and start steering toward that shape. So you tend harder, add one more word, hold the tone, keep the water moving, and the other person feels handled rather than met. What was meant to hold space starts clutching. What was meant to grow starts being managed. There is a point where the caring has already done its work, and that point is where you usually reach past it. The squeeze is not love and it is not the connection. Something already grew here. You will not lose it by letting it stand.

cells.tense: The door is closed, and you are still standing at it, facing the room you're in.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Take one pull that has been living in you without your consent — someone else's expectation, a direction you didn't choose — and write it on a scrap as borrowed. Leave the ones you chose unmarked.
cells.core: At that door, you were adjusting to other people's read of the situation more than your own, so the pull comes from several directions at once and you can't tell which one is yours. What feels like indecision there is closer to being overridden: too many hands on the blend, and you reaching for the last one who touched it. You have the sense for this. You did; you have just stopped trusting the read. What comes back first is not the old connection — it is knowing the difference between a pull you chose and a pull that was placed on you. That is small, and it is enough to find the door from the inside. You don't have to commit to a direction today. Only to see one you didn't author.

cells.tense: The pen is behind your back and you are already writing the direction they follow.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Someone near you is stuck where you have been. Rather than describing the way out, walk it beside them once — same pace, same ground — and stop when they stop.
cells.core: You adjust between people so smoothly that the adjusting has disappeared into the room — to hear it from you, the connection just happens, and no one is steering. It is not nothing. You are the one sensing when to add, when to step back, how to keep the two of you in one current so it keeps moving. The others feel it; they just don't know your name for it. Somewhere in there you began managing other people's direction instead of standing in your own, and the managing is called the connection. You are not a ghost at your own table. You are the one who keeps it level. Naming what you do is the first form of it — an earlier, plainer version of the steering, practice without the performance, that returns when you stop pretending you aren't doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You steer the room and say the room steers itself.

attempts.check: The signature is Bound, a decisive transient — I claim a chosen connection is being made, which the record supports only as the card, not as this person's history. The reader could say the connection isn't the point; what's true for them is the calibration itself, and they may recognise the flowing-choice as a thing they are weighing rather than making. The asks survive a wrong read because each is a small act the person can do regardless of who is in the room — defending a heading, resting in a result, telling their own pulls from borrowed ones, walking one route with someone. The line I serve myself with is 'two streams choosing one flow' — I have kept it out of the cores.
